newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton trade calls for early export quota.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton trade calls for early export quota.

text.p: Indian traders on Thursday sought early action on a parliamentary committee's suggestion that the government must release at least 10 million 170-kg bales of cotton for export ahead of the 1997/98 season, beginning October.
"It's a welcome suggestion and must be implemented immediately. But the export quota should be open to all," said a leading cotton trader.
The committee of law makers, which studied the problems of cotton growers, suggested that half the quota be given to the state-run Cotton Corporation of India.
Traders said the government should also announce a long-term export policy for cotton exports as India's production was expected to rise in the next few years.
Indian authorities recently announced that a technology mission launched in the current season would help boost productivity in the near future.
According to traders, prospects for the 1997/98 crop, which would come into the market in October, were bright.
The 1996/97 cotton crop has been estimated at 16.78 million bales, up from the previous year's 16.27 million.
Traders said cotton arrivals indicated that the current year's crop could even touch 17 million bales.
In the week to Thursday, cotton firmed on the local market on a shortage of ready stocks.
Expectations that the government might allow state-owned agencies to export more cotton also aided the firm tendency.
"Some state-owned agencies are nursing unsold stocks and are demanding permission to export more," one broker said.
Traders said India's cotton exports in 1996/97 were expected to be higher at 1.4 million bales compared with 790,000 bales in the previous season.
The government has already released 1.34 million bales for export in the current season, of which 1.15 million bales have been registered and 900,000 bales shipped.
India released 500,000 bales for export before the start of the current season and the move pushed prices up in a market saddled with huge carryover stocks from the previous year.

In spot, Bengal-deshi rose 40/65 rupees to 1,125/1,160 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), Punjab saw-ginned by 25 rupees to 1,830/1,900 rupees per maund and F-414 by 10 rupees to 2,080/2,100 rupees per maund.

Among Gujarat varieties, Kalyan cotton gained 300/400 rupees to 14,500/15,100 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) and Wagad cotton rose 500 rupees to 13,500 rupees per candy. Kala-ginned rose 300/400 rupees to 12,700 rupees per candy.
"This is just a usual rally at the tail end of the season and prices may ease in the coming days before the start of the new season," said Manubhai Amarsey, a leading cotton dealer.
"In some centres, scattered arrivals of the new crop from early sowing have already commenced," he said. "It is too early to predict the size of the new crop."
"The crop is very satisfactory," Amarsey said.
